answers.answer: HTTPX is a Python HTTP client library with synchronous/asynchronous APIs, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, plus an optional command-line client. Python applications call its exported functions/classes; shell users run the httpx console script (httpx:main). Repository tests also call it. These are evidenced entry surfaces, not an inventory of downstream users or proof of runtime execution.

__init__.py exposes the public facade; _api.py supplies convenience request functions; _client.py owns reusable sync/async clients and request orchestration. _models.py represents requests/responses, headers and cookies; _urls.py handles URLs/query parameters. _auth.py supplies authentication flows. _transports provides transport interfaces, httpcore-backed network adapters, in-process ASGI/WSGI adapters and mocks. _main.py implements the CLI. These are source modules/responsibilities, not separately distributed packages.

The implementation and tests are Python; Python >=3.9 is required. pyproject.toml uses Hatchling (hatchling.build) with hatch-fancy-pypi-readme; version comes from httpx/__version__.py and README/CHANGELOG supply package metadata. One distribution/import package, httpx, contains internal modules and _transports; tests are auxiliary code, included in the source distribution rather than a second product package. Required dependencies include httpcore==1.*, anyio, certifi and idna; CLI/HTTP2/SOCKS/compression integrations are optional extras.

The selected library entry begins at httpx.get, re-exported by httpx/__init__.py from _api.py. _api.get (174-207) calls request('GET', url, ...). _api.request (39-120) creates a context-managed Client and calls client.request. This is a library call, not the CLI main; follow_redirects defaults to False.
BaseClient._redirect_method in _client.py:494-515: 303 and 302 change every non-HEAD method to GET; 301 changes POST to GET. Otherwise preserve the method, including HEAD and 307/308.

Direct imports: _auth (Auth, BasicAuth, FunctionAuth); _models (Cookies, Headers, Request, Response); _transports.base (BaseTransport/AsyncBaseTransport); _transports.default (HTTPTransport/AsyncHTTPTransport). _urls and _utils support URL-based dispatch.

Client.request → build_request → send → _build_request_auth → _send_handling_auth (auth.sync_auth_flow/next) → _send_handling_redirects → request hooks → _send_single_request → _transport_for_url → transport.handle_request. After response hooks: has_redirect_location → _build_redirect_request → method/URL/headers/stream helpers → Request. Append history; follow_redirects=True reads the response and repeats with that request, subject to max_redirects. Dynamic boundaries: auth generators, hooks, overridden methods, mount/proxy/custom transport selection and streaming I/O. Default HTTPTransport calls external httpcore; the map is not runtime execution evidence.

Direct consumer: BaseClient._build_redirect_request, calling self._redirect_method at line 480. Indirect effects reach sync/async redirect loops, outgoing methods, body/header handling, convenience APIs and redirect tests. Runtime subclasses can override dispatch.

tests/client/test_redirects.py::test_redirect_301 (116-121) builds Client(transport=MockTransport(redirects)), then client.post('https://example.org/redirect_301', follow_redirects=True). The local redirects handler returns 301 with Location=https://example.org/; the next request receives its ordinary 200 response. MockTransport.handle_request reads the request and calls its supplied handler, so no network is needed. The test asserts 200, destination URL and one history entry; it exercises the POST→GET branch but does not explicitly assert the rewritten method.

Response.has_redirect_location requires 301/302/303/307/308 plus Location. _build_redirect_request calls _redirect_url: read response.headers['Location'], parse URL, translate InvalidURL to RemoteProtocolError, repair a scheme-without-host, resolve relative URLs, inherit a missing fragment, then pass the result to Request. URL.join uses urllib.parse.urljoin. With default networking, transport response headers enter through Response(headers=resp.headers).
